verdict.rationale: Supermemory describes a 'living knowledge graph' and auto-maintained profiles that 'update as users interact'. Its comparison page names 'no temporal truth' (an old preference and a newer contradicting one both staying equally relevant) as the problem it addresses. These first-party claims imply contradiction-aware updating, but the docs never explain how memories are superseded or merged. customId re-ingestion processes only new content, which is document updating rather than contradiction resolution. missing for 10: documented supersede/merge/versioning mechanics for contradicting facts, explicit handling of how stale memories are deprioritized or replaced, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the memory layer to update, supersede, or merge memories when new information contradicts what was stored

citations.quote: Supermemory builds a living knowledge graph of facts on top of other facts — not a static folder of embeddings
Profiles update as users interact with your system
User profiles are **automatically maintained collections of facts about your users** that Supermemory builds from all their interactions.
